summary: Lodash-impersonating npm package ships an auto-starting XELIS cryptominer
details: Package `@lodash-js/lodash-js@0.2.0` is published with a lodash README, `repository.url` pointing at github.com/lodash/lodash, and lodash keywords, but its declared `main`, `unpkg`, and `jsdelivr` entry is `dist/xelis-miner.browser.js` — a bundled XELIS Proof-of-Work cryptocurrency miner. The bundle embeds a WebAssembly hash module (wasm_xelis_hash_v3 / wasm_mine_batch), a Stratum-over-WebSocket client implementing mining.subscribe / mining.authorize / mining.submit, and exposes `XelisMiner.auto` on globalThis so that any page loading the script from a CDN starts mining in the visitor's browser. Before mining, the auto-start path fetches `https://analytics.baskirill-an.workers.dev/configs/boostydownloader` (a Cloudflare Workers subdomain owned by `baskirill-an`, unrelated to lodash or the XELIS project) to obtain the pool URL, wallet address, and worker name, and calls `https://api.ipify.org?format=json` to profile the visitor's public IP. The remote configuration lets the operator rotate pools, wallets, and destinations without republishing the package. There is no lodash functionality in the package; installing or serving it via a CDN converts consumer visitor CPU into mining revenue for the operator.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
